plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked cellular reprogramming & Yamanaka factor funnel chart from Till & McCulloch (February 1961 Radiation Research 14: 213–222), Gurdon (December 1962 J. Embryol. Exp. Morphol. 10: 622–640), and Takahashi & Yamanaka (25 August 2006 Cell 126: 663–676) shows all ~200 human cell types sharing the same 3-billion-base-pair genome (~20,000 genes), where narrowing 24 embryonic candidate genes down to just 4 transcription factors (Oct3/4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc) erases epigenetic bookmarks and rewinds adult fibroblasts into pluripotent stem cells.

teach_overlay.label: 1 EGG → ~200 CELL TYPES (2M RED CELLS/S) ← REWOUND BY 4 YAMANAKA FACTORS (FROM 24 CANDIDATES OUT OF 20,000 GENES)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked cellular reprogramming & stem-cell hierarchy chart on period paper showing 1 fertilized egg → pluripotent embryonic stem cells (capable of becoming all ~200 human cell types) → multipotent adult hematopoietic stem cells (producing ~2 million red blood cells/second) ← rewound by Yamanaka's 4 transcription factors (from 24 candidates out of ~20,000 genes) back into Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells (iPSCs)
teach_overlay.scale: out of the twenty thousand genes in your DNA book, flipping just four master switches is enough to erase a skin cell's memory of what it is and rewind its clock all the way back to day one

teach_overlay.detail: Inked Waddington epigenetic landscape & reprogramming chart comparing normal one-way embryonic differentiation (totipotent/pluripotent summit → ~200 specialized adult cell valleys locked by DNA methylation and histone marks) against somatic cell nuclear transfer (Gurdon 1962) and 4-factor iPSC reprogramming (Yamanaka 2006) pushing the adult cell back to the pluripotent summit
teach_overlay.scale: for a hundred years biologists thought a specialized cell was like a boulder that had rolled to the bottom of a mountain and could never roll back up — until Gurdon and Yamanaka built a four-gene ski lift back to the top
